gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-work-sans: Tall and literary up top, Noto Serif Hebrew keeps its stems and hairlines in a gentle, readable ratio. Work Sans follows in a plain sans, every stroke drawn at one thickness, so the heading's modest shading stands out clearly.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-archivo: Archivo has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward rather than curling in. Noto Serif Hentaigana sits above it with a gentle weight gradient along each rounded stroke, which gives the plain sans below a nicely quiet partner.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-fs-asap: Refined is the first word that comes to mind for Noto Serif Hentaigana, with thin strokes that stay clear of hairlines. And Asap does the opposite job, setting a sans body whose height nearly matches the capitals.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-fs-epilogue: A towering x-height gives Noto Serif Hentaigana its stubby, carpenter's-pencil look, with stems just a touch thicker than the strokes between them. And Epilogue brings a wire-like monoline skeleton, the steady line of a drafting pen, under that softer serif.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-fs-fira-san: Fira Sans has a larger-than-usual x-height and straight-edged strokes with no thick and thin shift at all. But Noto Serif Hentaigana is the one with rhythm, its wide-mouthed c shapes and modest weight changes giving each heading word some movement.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-fs-public-s: Trustworthy is how Public Sans comes across, with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters. And Noto Serif Hentaigana above it keeps its stroke variation understated, so the sans body and the serif heading sit comfortably together.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, heavy-looking strip of sans text through the middle of each line. Over a long passage the letters feel held open rather than curled shut, while Noto Serif Hentaigana adds gently modulated strokes without sharp hairlines.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-general-san: Tall, wide-mouthed and softly shaded, Noto Serif Hentaigana makes a stately opening. General Sans takes over with steady pen pressure and an x-height that fills the line, so a long passage glides smoothly around each bend.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-manrope: Manrope keeps one line width from start to finish. Its bright open gaps at every curve contrast nicely with Noto Serif Hentaigana, whose gentle thick-thin rhythm gives the heading a literary touch that the sans-serif body deliberately lacks.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-montserrat: Approachable and geometric, Montserrat leaves lots of white space leading into each curve, with oversized e and a counters. Noto Serif Hentaigana brings hairline-free, moderately weighty strokes above it.
